note: Career district. Conformed to mapping.the_secret.json. Three resolver changes are required before this file resolves cleanly: mode 'none', per-character defaultWardrobe, and textLayer 'native'. See THE_INSTRUCTION_VISUAL_MANIFEST.md §1.
textLayerNote: Bubbles are OFF for the whole Career scenario. Dialogue and choices are carried by the native Flutter layer below the contained 16:9 artwork. Without this flag the resolver extracts quoted spans into bubbles, and ask2_qa variant[0] emits four — over anchors.bubbles.maxPerNode — which the composer throws on.
characterIdsNote: 'You' is deliberately unmapped. The player is never drawn. The only node declaring it (resolution) is forced to `absent` via modeOverrides, where character_id() is computed but unused.
settingTokensNote: 'desk' resolves to the evening room because both nodes that author visual.setting 'desk' are the Wednesday evening beats. The daytime desk is reached through locationTokens only. 'phone' is not mapped: its only node (ask4_ownership) is presentation.type 'messages' and returns null before any scene resolves.
locationTokensNote: Order is load-bearing: resolve_scene_token uses startswith and returns the first hit, so 'Your desk, Wednesday evening' must precede the bare 'Your desk' or every desk beat lands in the evening room. 'The office' last, because it prefixes five different locations that all mean the same room.
moodMapNote: 'careful' is unreachable — its only node (ask4_ownership) is 'messages'. Mapped anyway so a later presentation-type change cannot fail the build silently. Registers are named by posture, not emotion, per spec §5.
modeOverridesNote: escalate_bare is the deliberate blank the scenario's testPlaythrough 5 declares. 'none' is a positive assertion of intentional absence, not a missing entry. ask3_client_email (type 'email') and audit_email (no location, no character) would otherwise fall through classify_mode to 'scene' and throw. audit_ray_calls is a native call card; the empty-desk beat it would carry is already served by audit_reply two nodes later, so a near-duplicate frame is avoided rather than drawn.
nodeOverridesNote: The coat is a wardrobe, not a prop — 'coat already on' is the Act 1 pressure signal and it is the garment Ray is wearing. Same reasoning that moved 'jacket' out of The Secret's propSynonyms. ask3_reaction takes the right slot because it resolves to the same room, figure and register as ask2_reaction; without the slot change the player sees an identical frame twice.

ask1_reaction.note: record:1 — 'Not annoyed. Slightly puzzled.' The node-level mood is 'distracted'; the variant prose establishes something else.

ask2_reaction.note: record:2 — 'It isn't hostile. It's almost hurt.' Node-level mood is 'relieved', which this variant contradicts in prose. variantIndex 0 is the record:2 entry; record:1 is index 1 and keeps the default register.

exitBeatsNote: Neither absent node carries a departure line. audit_reply and resolution are both empty rooms with no one leaving them, so exitBeat resolves null.
montagePanelsNote: Three panels, not four: anchors.montage sets panelWidth 440 and gap 48, so four panels span 1904 on a 1600 canvas. The fourth absence (never asked about the follow-on workstream) is carried by the prose.
propNote: Only two objects in this scenario are placed in a room by the prose and moved between scenes: the laptop and the notepad. Everything else is either environment (the monitor carrying 'upload dialog' and 'completion date field'; the meeting room's closed door), wardrobe (the coat), or prose-only. 'a closed door' is deliberately NOT mapped to the existing prop.door_closed — that asset is a domestic kitchen door drawn for Neighbourhood, and reusing it in a corporate meeting room is a craft mismatch. The room draws its own, exactly as scene.coffee_shop draws its own window and espresso machine.
scoringKeysNote: No entry in this file names a state, score or derived key. registries.json scoring_keys_forbidden carries The Instruction's keys so negative_test.py can assert it.
